notes: CONFIRMED from the paper, not from the triage hint. 'All eligible clients registered with EPPIC between 1 January 2011 and 31 December 2016 were included'; 1220 presented, 1196 with complete place-of-birth data. One recruited cohort, split post hoc by country of birth, so one cohort_id with two subgroup arms and NOT two cohorts under D12.5: the split is not a second recruitment.

CONFIRMED as the Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966, the same cohort as the piloted rautio2016 and majuri2021: 'The study was based on the Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966 (NFBC1966), which is an unselected, general population sample comprising 12,058 live-born children with expected dates of birth in 1966 in the provinces of Oulu and Lapland' (Methods, Sample, p. 66). This corroborates the existing employment_selection_status = none on the cohort row in data/extraction_cohorts.csv; no change is proposed to that row. contributes_results = no: the report yields only latent employment-trajectory class membership over ages 16 to 45, which is not a prevalence at a timepoint. RESULT SELECTION ACROSS THE THREE NFBC1966 REPORTS RESOLVES TO NO CHANGE. There is no competing pair to choose between at any horizon: majuri2023 contributes no result at all; rautio2016's 18/161 is paid_intensity_threshold, period prevalence over a 24-month window, measured at chronological age 44-45 and therefore barred from every horizon by D12.3b; and majuri2021's 15/170 and 17/91 are an `unclear` construct with any_time_during_followup ascertainment on the dp_psychiatric subgroup arm, a different cell of (horizon, ascertainment, construct) again. Nothing in majuri2023 bears on rautio2016's '<25 per cent' band problem (D12.3) or on its age-anchored measurement (D12.3b), so neither finding is contradicted.

CONFIRMED. One recruited convenience sample of 53 people with schizophrenia drawn from two Sao Paulo outpatient services, all of whom completed the same prevocational training group. Employment-selected, so it can contribute only to a separately labelled selected-population analysis, and its only whole-cohort result is additionally blocked as unresolved.

CONFIRMED. 'The current paper presents a secondary analysis of data from a 24-month randomised trial' and 'The present analysis treats participants recruited to the trial as a single cohort', so relationship = secondary_analysis rather than describes; the main RADAR trial report is cited as reference 33. The whole-cohort EET row is derived by summing the two post-randomisation relapse subgroups, which partition the cohort exactly (82 + 171 = 253 entered, 66 + 124 = 190 observed); reconstructing the whole cohort is not the same as SELECTING a post-randomisation subgroup, which is what SAP 2.1 bars.
